cases.name: modulo-picks-every-second-row
cases.description: The condition everybody writes first. Before `%` existed this was unwritable in if=, and the only way through was a compute sequence holding <mod> — two metres away and invisible.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="P"><gen if="_count % 2 == 0" type="text" value="even"/><gen type="text" value="odd"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: modulo-is-euclidean-not-the-host-languages
cases.description: The case that catches a port reaching for its own `%`. Euclidean says -4 % 3 is 2; JavaScript, Java, C# and Rust all say -1. The compute layer's <mod> already answered 2, and one engine must not give two answers to one question.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="-4,-3,-2,-1,0" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="N % 3 == 0" type="text" value="0"/><gen if="N % 3 == 1" type="text" value="1"/><gen if="N % 3 == 2" type="text" value="2"/><gen type="text" value="?"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}%3=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: round-sends-a-half-away-from-zero
cases.description: Three hosts, three answers, none symmetric: JavaScript rounds a half toward +INF, Python rounds to even, Java rounds half up. TDC rounds away from zero, so a column of negatives behaves like a column of positives.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="0.5,-0.5,1.5,-1.5,2.5,-2.5" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="round(N) == 1" type="text" value="1"/><gen if="round(N) == 0 - 1" type="text" value="-1"/><gen if="round(N) == 2" type="text" value="2"/><gen if="round(N) == 0 - 2" type="text" value="-2"/><gen if="round(N) == 3" type="text" value="3"/><gen if="round(N) == 0 - 3" type="text" value="-3"/><gen type="text" value="?"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>round(${{N}})=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: abs-floor-ceil-trunc-on-a-negative-fraction
cases.description: floor and trunc part company on negatives — floor(-7.5) is -8, trunc(-7.5) is -7 — which is exactly where a port that reached for the wrong one goes unnoticed.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen if="abs(0 - 7.5) == 7.5" type="text" value="abs=ok"/><gen type="text" value="abs=BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="F"><gen if="floor(0 - 7.5) == 0 - 8" type="text" value="floor=ok"/><gen type="text" value="floor=BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen if="ceil(0 - 7.5) == 0 - 7" type="text" value="ceil=ok"/><gen type="text" value="ceil=BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="T"><gen if="trunc(0 - 7.5) == 0 - 7" type="text" value="trunc=ok"/><gen type="text" value="trunc=BAD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}} ${{F}} ${{C}} ${{T}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: min-and-max-are-variadic-and-compose
cases.description: Functions nest inside each other and inside the operators, so a port cannot get away with a flat special case per name.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="-9,4,-2" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="max(abs(N), 3) % 2 == 1" type="text" value="odd-max"/><gen if="min(abs(N), 3) == 3" type="text" value="min-is-3"/><gen type="text" value="other"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>N=${{N}} -> ${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-row-counter-is-a-number-past-the-ninth-row
cases.description: _count used to arrive as text, and coerceInt lets a SINGLE digit through — so this config ran to row 9 and threw on row 10. Twelve rows is the shortest run that proves it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="12" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="P"><compute><result><mod><field name="_count"/><int v="5"/></mod></result></compute></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{_count}}:${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: in-tests-membership-of-a-bare-word-list
cases.description: The alternative says the column name once per value and grows a term per country. Bare words inside the list stay bare, the way the rest of the language reads an unquoted word.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C"><gen type="text" value="US,FR,CA,JP,MX" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="C in [US, CA, MX]" type="text" value="NAFTA"/><gen type="text" value="other"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{C}}=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: in-compares-as-loosely-as-equals-does
cases.description: The column is text and the list is numbers. `==` already bridges that, so `in` must not be stricter — the two would disagree about the same pair.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="1,3,7" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="N in [1, 2, 3]" type="text" value="in"/><gen type="text" value="out"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: string-predicates-read-a-value-as-text
cases.description: starts_with, ends_with, contains and len over one column of surnames — the four an author reaches for before any arithmetic.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="McDonald,OBrien,Li,Rodriguez" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="starts_with(N, Mc)" type="text" value="prefix"/><gen if="len(N) < 3" type="text" value="short"/><gen if="contains(N, rig)" type="text" value="inside"/><gen if="ends_with(N, ien)" type="text" value="suffix"/><gen type="text" value="."/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: len-counts-code-points-and-never-numbers
cases.description: Two decisions in one case. An emoji is ONE code point, not the two UTF-16 units JavaScript would report — Python's len() and Rust's chars().count() already agree, and Java and C# reach it with codePointCount. And "10" is two characters rather than the number ten, which is what keeps the string family separate from the numeric one.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="S"><gen type="text" value="ab,😀ab,10" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="len(S) == 2" type="text" value="2"/><gen if="len(S) == 3" type="text" value="3"/><gen type="text" value="?"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>[${{S}}] len=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: upper-lower-and-is-empty
cases.description: An empty column is falsy already; is_empty says so out loud, which a reader can see is deliberate rather than a forgotten condition.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="S"><gen type="text" value="aB,,CD" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="is_empty(S)" type="text" value="empty"/><gen if="upper(S) == AB" type="text" value="up-AB"/><gen if="lower(S) == cd" type="text" value="low-cd"/><gen type="text" value="?"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>[${{S}}]=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-ternary-picks-a-value-then-it-is-compared
cases.description: The ternary produces a VALUE, not a branch of the config — what surrounds it is an ordinary comparison.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="N"><gen type="text" value="10,50,90" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="(N > 40 ? N : 0) > 60" type="text" value="high"/><gen if="(N > 40 ? N : 0) > 0" type="text" value="mid"/><gen type="text" value="low"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}=${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: tdcmath-produces-the-same-double-everywhere
cases.description: A bit-level pin wearing the clothes of a behaviour case. Each literal is the exact double TdcMath produces, and `==` on doubles is true only when every bit matches — so an implementation that reached for its host libm prints SQRT-BAD or COS-BAD rather than passing quietly. cos(1000) and tan(1) are here by name: those are two of the values measured to differ between Node and Python on one machine.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen if="sqrt(2) == 1.4142135623730951" type="text" value="sqrt"/><gen type="text" value="SQRT-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen if="exp(1) == 2.7182818284590455" type="text" value="exp"/><gen type="text" value="EXP-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen if="log(7) == 1.9459101490553132" type="text" value="log"/><gen type="text" value="LOG-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="D"><gen if="sin(1) == 0.8414709848078965" type="text" value="sin"/><gen type="text" value="SIN-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="E"><gen if="cos(1000) == 0.5623790762907029" type="text" value="cos"/><gen type="text" value="COS-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="F"><gen if="tan(1) == 1.557407724654902" type="text" value="tan"/><gen type="text" value="TAN-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="G"><gen if="pow(7, 2.5) == 129.64181424216497" type="text" value="pow"/><gen type="text" value="POW-BAD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}} ${{B}} ${{C}} ${{D}} ${{E}} ${{F}} ${{G}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: sqrt exp log sin cos tan pow

cases.name: tdcmath-second-wave-produces-the-same-double-everywhere
cases.description: The same bit-level pin as the first wave, for the inverses and hyperbolics. Each literal is the exact double TdcMath produces, and `==` on doubles is true only when every bit matches, so a port that reached for its host libm prints ATAN-BAD or CBRT-BAD instead of passing quietly. atan2(3, -4) is here because the quadrant cannot be recovered from the ratio alone, and cbrt(10) because cbrt is not pow(x, 1/3): one third is not a double.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen if="atan(2) == 1.1071487177940904" type="text" value="atan"/><gen type="text" value="ATAN-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen if="asin(0.7) == 0.7753974966107531" type="text" value="asin"/><gen type="text" value="ASIN-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen if="acos(0.3) == 1.266103672779499" type="text" value="acos"/><gen type="text" value="ACOS-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="D"><gen if="atan2(3, -4) == 2.498091544796509" type="text" value="atan2"/><gen type="text" value="ATAN2-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="E"><gen if="sinh(2) == 3.626860407847019" type="text" value="sinh"/><gen type="text" value="SINH-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="F"><gen if="cosh(3) == 10.067661995777765" type="text" value="cosh"/><gen type="text" value="COSH-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="G"><gen if="tanh(0.5) == 0.4621171572600098" type="text" value="tanh"/><gen type="text" value="TANH-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="H"><gen if="cbrt(10) == 2.154434690031884" type="text" value="cbrt"/><gen type="text" value="CBRT-BAD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}} ${{B}} ${{C}} ${{D}} ${{E}} ${{F}} ${{G}} ${{H}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: atan asin acos atan2 sinh cosh tanh cbrt

cases.name: tdcmath-third-wave-produces-the-same-double-everywhere
cases.description: The bit-level pin for the cancellation-avoiding shapes, and the arguments are not decorative. The first six were CHOSEN because the host libm disagrees with TdcMath there in both Rust and Python — a pin at a point where every implementation already agrees proves nothing, which is how the first draft of this case was written and why it was replaced. hypot is pinned at 1e200 instead: it agrees with the hosts everywhere sampled, being built from sqrt, but the naive sqrt(x*x + y*y) overflows to infinity there, so this line catches the mistake the function exists to prevent.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen if="expm1(0.625) == 0.8682459574322223" type="text" value="expm1"/><gen type="text" value="EXPM1-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen if="log1p(0.25) == 0.22314355131420974" type="text" value="log1p"/><gen type="text" value="LOG1P-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen if="log2(0.625) == -0.6780719051126376" type="text" value="log2"/><gen type="text" value="LOG2-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="D"><gen if="asinh(0.125) == 0.12467674692144275" type="text" value="asinh"/><gen type="text" value="ASINH-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="E"><gen if="acosh(1.04) == 0.28190828905414694" type="text" value="acosh"/><gen type="text" value="ACOSH-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="F"><gen if="atanh(0.002) == 0.002000002666673067" type="text" value="atanh"/><gen type="text" value="ATANH-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="G"><gen if="hypot(1e200, 1e200) == 1.414213562373095e+200" type="text" value="hypot"/><gen type="text" value="HYPOT-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="H"><gen if="sign(-7) == -1" type="text" value="sign"/><gen type="text" value="SIGN-BAD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}} ${{B}} ${{C}} ${{D}} ${{E}} ${{F}} ${{G}} ${{H}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: expm1 log1p log2 asinh acosh atanh hypot sign

cases.name: a-number-may-carry-an-exponent
cases.description: Scientific notation in an if expression, which four of the five implementations could not read. `1e6` lexed as the number 1 followed by the name `e6`, and the parser then complained about unbalanced parentheses — a message about the wrong thing entirely. It went unseen because no shared case had ever written a literal that way. All four forms are here: bare exponent, explicit plus, explicit minus, and capital E.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="ex" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="A"><gen if="1e6 == 1000000" type="text" value="bare"/><gen type="text" value="BARE-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen if="2.5e+3 == 2500" type="text" value="plus"/><gen type="text" value="PLUS-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen if="5e-3 == 0.005" type="text" value="minus"/><gen type="text" value="MINUS-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="D"><gen if="1.5E2 == 150" type="text" value="capital"/><gen type="text" value="CAPITAL-BAD"/></sequence><sequence name="E"><gen if="len(e6) == 2" type="text" value="name-intact"/><gen type="text" value="NAME-BAD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}} ${{B}} ${{C}} ${{D}} ${{E}}</data></line></block></tdc>
